 5. Mr. SR Karmaker, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the plaintiffs having themselves prayed for a decree for declaration of the kabala of the defendant opposite party as collusive and void, they should have valued the suit according to the value of the property as mentioned in the impugned kabala. The learned Advocate submits that though objective standard for valuation of the suit is readily available the plaintiffs have wrongly valued the suit according to their own standard as derived from the kabala executed in their favour. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Munsif committed a substantial error of law in failing to consider that while an objection is raised by the defendant as to the valuation of the relief sought, it was the duty cast upon the court under section 8C of the Court Fees Act to hold an enquiry and to determine the correct valuation particularly when an objective standard of valuation is available from the kabala of the defendants under challenge. The learned Advocate also submits that in the present case an objective standard for valuation of the relief sought for by way of khas possession being clearly available and the said valuation, if properly assessed after necessary enquiry, may exceed the pecuniary jurisdiction of the court concerned and, therefore, the learned Munsif committed an error of law in putting off the valuation matter to be disposed of at the time of per-emptory hearing of the suit along with other issues. In support of his contention Mr. SR Karmaker has relied on the case of Keramat Ali Vs.
